title: RetroArch in a browser, from a container

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if you could open a retro game emulator in any browser, with nothing to install?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's what this project packages. It takes a WebAssembly build of RetroArch and wraps it in a Docker container, so the emulator runs straight in the browser.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The browser runtime files, plus scripts and the container assembly that put it all together for a static web server. Antoine's note makes a clear point: hosting the player and supplying game content are separate concerns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the repo is the player, not the games.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. It's a neat way to show how an emulator can be shipped as a simple web bundle. The project is MIT licensed, now archived.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The written page has more on how it's assembled.
